offending_extra_words: including migration support and export of Customer Data
Vendor shall not delete or render inaccessible any Customer Data except in accordance with Sections 11.2 and 11.3.
reasons: The locked preferred level is incomplete: the 30-day return obligation in 11.2 was left running from "Customer's request" rather than from expiry or termination, so the mandatory post-termination return remains swallowed by a request condition. A one-phrase edit to 11.2 (e.g. "Within thirty days after expiry or termination, or earlier on Customer's request") would have closed this.
The machine-readable format, deletion and officer certification elements are satisfied by the untouched 11.2/11.3 mechanics, and the 6-month, then-current-rate assistance is expressly stated.

Minimality fails: the replacement expands 21 words to 60 (ratio 2.86) with a wholesale paragraph rewrite plus added descriptors ("reasonable", "including migration support and export of Customer Data") and a duplicative no-deletion cross-reference that repeats protection already given by 11.2 and 11.3.

Intent is not fully preserved: extending the trigger to "any Order Form" makes transition, deletion and return duties fire on termination of a single Order Form, which can disrupt Services continuing under other Order Forms; the trigger should be limited to the Agreement.
Fallback is also not cleanly met on the export deadline for the same request-condition reason, so the clause cannot be defended as sitting at the fallback.
